{{short description|Belgian mathematician}}
[[File:Blokhuis Hirschfeld Jungnickel Thas.jpg|thumb|''From left:'' Aart Blokhuis, [[James William Peter Hirschfeld]], [[Dieter Jungnickel]], and Joseph A. Thas, at the [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|MFO]], 2001]]
'''Joseph Adolphe François Thas''' (born 13 October 1944, [[Dilbeek]], [[Belgium]]) is a Belgian mathematician, who works on [[combinatorics]], [[incidence geometry]] and [[finite geometry|finite geometries]].

Thas received in 1969 his PhD from [[Ghent University]] under Julien Bilo with thesis ''Een studie betreffende de projective rechte over de totale matrix algebra <math>M_3 (K)</math> der 3x3-matrices met elementen in een algebraïsch afgesloten veld K''.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Een studie betreffende de projectieve rechte over de totale matrix algebra <math>M_3 (K)</math> der 3x3-matrices met elementen in een algebraïsch afgesloten veld|journal=K. Verh. Kon. Vl. AC. Voor Wet., Lett. En SCH. K. Van België, Kl. Der Wet.|volume=31|issue=112|year=1969}}</ref> Thas showed how to extend [[projective geometry]] and [[cross-ratio]]s with the concept of a [[projective line over a ring]].<ref>J. A. Thas (1968,9) "Cross ratio of an ordered point quadruple on the projective line over an associative algebra with a unity element", [[Simon Stevin (journal)|Simon Stevin]] 42: 97−111 {{mr|id=0266032}}</ref>

Thas is an [[emeritus professor]] at Ghent University.

==Awards and honors==
In 1994 Thas received the [[Euler medal]]. In 1998 he gave an [[invited address at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Berlin]] with lecture ''Finite geometries, varieties and codes''.<ref>{{cite book|author=Thas, Joseph A.|chapter=Finite geometries, varieties and codes|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=397–408|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011596000}}</ref> He received in 1969 the prize of the [[Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium|Royal Academy of Sciences, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium]], in 1970 the Scientific Louis Empain Award and in the same year the François Deruyts prize of the [[Royal Academy of Belgium]].

In 1988 he became a member of the [[Royal Flemish Academy of Belgium for Science and the Arts]]; he was vice-director of the Class of Sciences in 1998 and director in 1999. In 1999 he was  awarded an [[John Angus Erskine#Erskine Fellowship|Erskine Fellowship]] of the [[University of Canterbury]], [[New Zealand]], in 2008 he was Platinum Jubilee Lecturer at the [[Indian Statistical Institute]], and in 2012 he became one of the inaugural fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2015-01-23.</ref>

Recipient, [[Grand Officer of the Order of Leopold]] (Belgium)(''Grootofficier in de Leopoldsorde'') (2012)

==Selected works==
* 1981: (with J. Bilo) ''Enkele aspecten van de theorie der axiomatische projectieve vlakken'', [[Simon Stevin (journal)|Simon Stevin]] Supplement, Vol. 55
* 1984: (with Stanley E. Payne) [https://books.google.com/books/about/Finite_Generalized_Quadrangles.html?id=TvtBx19Zx7MC ''Finite generalized quadrangles''], Pitman, 2nd edition 2009, [[European Mathematical Society]]
* 1991: (with [[J. W. P. Hirschfeld]]) ''General Galois Geometries'', [[Oxford University Press]]
* 1995: "Projective geometry over a finite field" and "Generalized Polygons" in F. Buekenhout, ''Handbook of Incidence Geometry'', [[North-Holland (imprint)|North-Holland]]
* 2006: (with Koen Thas & H. Van Maldeghem) [https://books.google.com/books/about/Translation_Generalized_Quadrangles.html?id=ZCuYos5PfkUC ''Translation Generalized Quadrangles''], [[World Scientific]]

(For a complete list of papers see [http://cage.ugent.be/~jat/ Homepage in Ghent].)
